name: NVIDIA DGX B300, MLPerf Inference v6.1 Server: Llama 2 70B on 8x B300-SXM-270GB, aggregate output throughput under the Server latency constraint
unit: output tokens/s (aggregate, harness 'Completed tokens per second')
methodology: AGGREGATE. MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed division, Datacenter suite, SERVER scenario, which is a materially different measurement from Offline on identical hardware. LOADS: target_qps 0.5 (llama2-70b/user.conf '*.Server.target_qps = 0.5', Poisson arrivals), min_duration 120000 ms, min_query_count 100, plus the compiled-in per-query TTFT and TPOT 99th-percentile bounds which the log reports as 'Performance constraints satisfied : Yes' and 'TTFT/TPOT Early Stopping Result: Run successful'. Batch size is not a fixed published number - the submitter's scheduler adapts it - but it is bounded by what the latency constraint permits, which is exactly why Server lands below Offline. Completed samples per second 391.79. Model shape TOKENS_PER_SAMPLE 267.0. POWER: has_power=False, design_power_watts=null, no declared cap. OMITTED BY SOURCE: the numeric TTFT/TPOT bounds applied (they are compiled into the harness for this model/scenario and are not written into user.conf or the log), TP size, KV dtype, concurrency.
notes: This is the number to use when someone asks 'how fast can this node serve Llama 2 70B', because it is the only one carrying a latency guarantee. The 2.2% discount versus Offline (109277) is the measured price of holding a tail-latency bound. Note the direction of the claim: this is an AGGREGATE throughput with a per-query latency bound satisfied, NOT a per-user tok/s figure - the harness does not expose a tok/s-per-user metric for the Server scenario in these logs.
